home.tagline: Open source AI agents that build software

quickstart.title: Get started in 60 seconds
quickstart.desc: Clone, install dependencies, spin up Redis + ChromaDB, and start the local server.

workflow.title: How It Works
workflow.desc: From conversation to working code. A 4-step AI agent workflow.
workflow.step1Desc: Turn ideas into a PRD through conversation. The agent asks clarifying questions and produces a refined spec.
workflow.step2Desc: Analyzes the PRD and Figma designs to generate UI tokens, asset inventories, and component spec documents. System design (API contracts, etc.) is also included.
workflow.step3Desc: Generates real code from design documents. Automatically diagnoses and fixes build failures, and runs tasks in parallel.
workflow.step4Desc: Preview generated code in real time. See results instantly and iterate with feedback.

features.title: What you get
features.multiAgentDesc: Planner, Architect, Runtime — separate agents for separate concerns. Each owns its phase.
features.parallelDesc: Tasks run in parallel by default. Foundation tasks block, integration tasks fan out.
features.figmaDesc: Reads Figma designs directly via MCP — actual component structure, variables, and styles.
features.stackDesc: TypeScript, JavaScript, and Go today. Python, Java, Rust planned (PRs welcome).
features.selfHostDesc: Same architecture in both modes — Redis + BullMQ + Pub/Sub. No silent fallbacks.
features.localDesc: Vector DB optional. Live preview in the browser. Bring your own LLM key.

demo.desc: A short walkthrough of the Plan → Design → Code → Preview loop.

items.a: Apache-2.0. You can self-host, fork, modify, and use ANT in commercial products. The full text lives at /LICENSE in the repo.
No telemetry. The self-host build does not call out except for LLM API requests you initiate. The cloud build only stores what you create in your workspace.
Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, and Bedrock are wired in today. The provider adapter is small — adding a new provider is a contribution-friendly task.
Redis and ChromaDB (both via docker compose). Node 20+, pnpm 10+. The dev script spins everything up locally.
ANT Cloud is the managed deployment of the same OSS code. Same agents, same workflow — we just run the infra. See the Cloud page.
Yes. Workspaces are stored on disk in standard formats (Markdown, JSON). Export from cloud, point self-host at the directory, done.

selfHost.heroDesc: Self-host on your own machine — Redis in Docker, four Ant processes, your own LLM key. No OAuth, no Kubernetes, no managed account.
selfHost.infraDesc: Local mode is a distributed system on a single machine. Same architecture as cloud — only the topology differs.

process.api: API server (port 4100) — receives requests, enqueues jobs
process.worker: Job worker — runs LangGraph agents in child processes
process.realtime: Realtime SSE server (port 4101) — streams agent state to the UI

infraDeps.title: Infrastructure
infraDeps.chroma: Optional — ChromaDB vector index. Off by default; the RAG chain falls back to git-changes + keyword search.

selfHost.envDesc: Local mode skips OAuth, JWT, and CORS allowlists entirely. Four values do the job.

env.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
env.desc: Or another LLM key (OPENAI_API_KEY, AWS Bedrock)

selfHost.llmDesc: Local mode doesn't proxy LLM calls. Set one of these.
selfHost.uiTitle: What the UI looks like in local mode
selfHost.uiDesc: The GNB shows a Local Org / Local User badge where Sign In normally sits in cloud mode. ANT_SERVER_MODE on the backend is the single source of truth — there is no mode toggle in the UI. No sign-up screen either; everything belongs to a single fixed local:local tenant.
selfHost.nextStepsDesc: Step-by-step prerequisites, env reference, the optional vector DB, and troubleshooting live in the repo.

faq.q: How is this different from self-host?
faq.a: Same exact code. The only differences are infrastructure (we run it) and authentication (Google sign-in instead of localhost). Workspaces are interchangeable.
ANT Cloud meters usage in credits. Every plan includes a monthly credit allotment, and you can top up anytime. The Free plan is enough to evaluate — see the Plans & credits section for details.

faq.q: Can I migrate from cloud to self-host?
faq.a: Yes. Workspaces are stored as Markdown and JSON on disk. Export from cloud, point self-host at the directory, done.
Workspace data lives on managed, EFS-backed storage. Self-host if you need specific data-residency guarantees.
Right here — see the Plans & credits section below. The OSS self-host build is free forever.

figma.heroDesc: Not screenshot capture. AI directly reads and analyzes Figma's actual component structure, design tokens, and variables.
figma.gen1Desc: Design token definitions (color palette, typography scale, spacing system)
figma.step1Desc: Figma Desktop is required. MCP access is not available through the web version.
figma.step2Desc: Ant Desktop is a bridge connecting your local Figma to ANT (cloud or self-host). Install it, run it from the system tray, and it will auto-pair with your ANT instance.
figma.step3Title: Connect Figma URL in your project
figma.step3Desc: Enter the Figma file URL when creating a feature. Run the Design job → ANT explores Figma data → design documents are generated.

faqItems.q: Does it work with Figma web?
faqItems.a: No. Figma Desktop App is required for MCP access.

faqItems.q: Does Ant Desktop have write access to Figma?
faqItems.a: No. Read-only. It only analyzes design data and never modifies Figma files.

faqItems.q: Can I use ANT without Figma?
faqItems.a: Yes. Upload reference images (screenshots) or use text descriptions only. Figma integration is an option for more accurate results.

capabilities.heroDesc: ANT is not tied to any specific language or framework. It analyzes your project's tech stack and generates tailored code.
capabilities.monorepoDesc: Turborepo, pnpm workspace, and other multi-package setups
capabilities.langTs: Broadest support. The entire React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Node.js ecosystem.
capabilities.langGo: Standard library servers, Gin, Echo, etc.
capabilities.langPy: Django, FastAPI, Flask, and general Python projects.
capabilities.langRust: Axum, Actix, and other web frameworks.
capabilities.howDesc: ANT doesn't use fixed templates. It learns your project's existing code — coding conventions, directory structure, dependencies — then generates code in a consistent style.
capabilities.note: Currently supports TypeScript/JavaScript and Go. Python, Java/Kotlin, and Rust are open for contributions — the language adapter is small and well-isolated.

download.heroDesc: Two ways to install Ant today: build from source for the full local-mode experience, or wait for the desktop bridge app.
download.sourceDesc: Clone, install, run. Three steps and Ant is live on your laptop in local mode.
download.sourcePrereqMac: macOS — Node 20+ (brew install node@20), pnpm 10+, Docker Desktop
download.sourcePrereqWin: Windows — WSL2 recommended; Node 20+, pnpm 10+, Docker Desktop
download.sourcePrereqLinux: Linux — Node 20+ (distro or NodeSource), pnpm 10+, Docker
download.desktopDesc: A small tray-app bridge between your local Figma Desktop and Ant. Signed binaries are in progress — for now, build from source above.
download.comingSoonToast: We're working on signed binaries — build from source above for now.
download.whatTitle: What the desktop app will do
download.whatDesc: A bridge between your local environment and your Ant instance.
download.bridgeDesc: Securely relays design data from Figma Desktop to Ant. Outbound connections only — no inbound ports opened.
download.trayDesc: Runs quietly in the system tray. Only relays Figma data on demand, using minimal resources.
download.monitorDesc: Live status of your Ant and Figma Desktop connection.
download.codeSignNotice: Ant Desktop binaries will be signed before the public release. Until then, build from source above is the recommended path.
